findings.finding: The test title claims a 'compact (non-oversized) status link', but it only asserts that an svg exists inside .mc-story-link. jsdom does not load CSS, and the svg was already there before this change, so the test cannot fail if the 1em sizing rule is removed. The real proof is the bounding-box check in client/e2e/flows/mission-subrunner.spec.ts:129-132.
findings.suggestion: Rename the test so it claims only what it checks (the visible title plus the glyph inside the link), and point to the e2e spec for the size check. Or remove the svg assertion.

findings.finding: `[data-kind="blocker"]` toHaveCount(0) can never fail now that the 'blocker' kind no longer exists. AC1 also says 'no raw output', but the spec never checks that the seeded error text ('! [rejected]') is absent. Only the unit test checks this, via `detail` being undefined.
findings.suggestion: Replace or supplement the check with `await expect(feed).not.toContainText("[rejected]")` so the browser test actually catches the raw output coming back.

findings.finding: Both Read cards in this fixture are wordless, so the reconcile filter drops them and `cards` is empty. `cards.every(...)` and `!cards.some(...)` are then true on an empty list. The test still catches a returning error card, but it passes for the wrong reason and would not notice a card that is not an error but carries leaked detail.
findings.suggestion: Add narration to the turn so the card survives the filter, then assert on that specific card (status undefined, detail undefined, both command chips present). Or explicitly assert `cards.length`.

findings.finding: `PendingTool.commandKey` (tool name plus command detail) was only read by the removed blocker-recovery code. Now the only reader is `applySubrunnerAck`, which needs just the tool name and gets its own key at line 186. The keys built at lines 194/232/244/288 for non-subrunner tools are never read. The file name `missionActivityFeedBlockerAndTdd.test.ts` is also stale now that blockers are gone.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking boy-scout fix: build commandKey only for subrunner dispatches (or make it optional), and rename the test file to e.g. `missionActivityFeedTdd.test.ts` together with the three comments that cite it (AuthoringRollback.ts:10, AuthoringRollback.test.ts:3, AuthoringTrack.ts:20, GateSynthesis.test.ts:3).

findings.finding: Behaviour change that is not documented: the removed recovery path used to merge a successful retry (same command) into the earlier failed card and drop the duplicate. Now a failed narrated command and its successful retry show up as two ordinary cards, unless add() coalesces them. This is consistent with 'no errors in the feed', but the visible duplicate is not mentioned in the mini-plan.
findings.suggestion: Either accept it and record it in the mini-plan or decision drop, or add a unit test that pins the fail-then-retry shape so the result is a deliberate choice.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the subrunner status glyph now renders at line size, inline in the link row — client/src/index.css:1 does `@import "tailwindcss"`, which includes Tailwind 4 preflight (`svg { display:block; vertical-align:middle }`). The new rule `.mc-story-link svg { width:1em; height:1em; margin-right:5px; vertical-align:-.125em }` (mission-operation.css:61) never resets `display`, and `.mc-story-link` itself is a plain button, not flex/inline-flex. The likely result is that the 1em check or X sits on its OWN line above 'View subrunner report' / 'View failure details': `vertical-align` and `margin-right` would do nothing on a block box. That is not the compact single row the spec asks for. The unit test (MissionActivityFeedCard.test.tsx:201) only asserts that `.mc-story-link svg` exists. jsdom applies no CSS, so it cannot catch this, and no E2E or visual check measures the geometry. Every sibling icon host in this file (`.mc-feed-pill`, `.mc-feed-chip`, `.mc-feed-subrunner-status`, `.mc-gate-btn`) uses `display:inline-flex` for exactly this reason.
findings.suggestion: Add `display:inline-block` to the svg (or make `.mc-story-link` `inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px` for this usage only). Prove it in a real browser: icon top within the text line box, icon height of about 1em. Per the memory notes, a layout fix needs a vitest class fence plus a real-browser E2E.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: 'No error messages in the chat at all; errors are handled in the terminal' is satisfied — The spec's only explicit carve-out is 'genuine interactive blockers or questions — keep those'. The mini-plan's AC3 widened that carve-out on its own authority. A failing test command still gets a red 'Failing' pill, an XIcon and the raw FAIL output in a `<pre>` (Resolve.ts:127-128, attachDetail). A failed subrunner still renders 'View failure details' with an X. Read literally, those are error messages in the chat. The defensible reading (a test verdict is a verification result, not an error message) is reasonable, but the user never made it, and Sven's wording ('at all') is absolute.
findings.suggestion: State the interpretation explicitly in the PR body and the iterate record: test verdicts and subagent outcomes are kept as status, not as error messages. Alternatively, confirm with the user in plain language: 'Should a failing test still show as a red Failing card with its output, or should that also live only in the terminal?'

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: removing the recovery merge is harmless — A failed plain command now keeps its card unmutated: same kind, no status, command chip intact. A retry in a later turn makes a second card with an identical chip. In the feed, `git push` (rejected) followed by `git push` (ok) reads as two pushes that both succeeded, with nothing marking the first as failed. Before this change, that sequence collapsed into one 'recovered' card. This follows directly from the stated intent (errors live in the terminal), so it is not a defect, but it is misleading-by-omission. `PendingTool.commandKey` is now only used by the subrunner path (split to recover the dispatch tool name), so it survives as a misleadingly general field.
findings.suggestion: Accept and record it as a known trade-off. Optionally narrow or rename `commandKey` so it is not mistaken for a live dedupe key.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: review-bucket failures degrade gracefully — A review `Task` whose tool_result is_error used to become a blocker card. It now hits the generic `continue` before the review branch, so the card shows 'Spawned X to review the change.' with no detail and no status, permanently. It looks the same as a review still in flight or one that returned nothing. This is consistent with M1's intent, but no test pins it.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test for an errored review Task: no err status, no detail, card still present. That fixes the behavior so it cannot drift.

findings.finding: The spec says "Verify the same logic does not also drive genuine interactive blockers or questions and keep those." The removed `handleGenericBlockerError` was the generic catch-all for every `is_error` tool_result outside the test/subrunner/review branches. This diff replaces it with an unconditional `continue` and contains no test or code demonstrating that an interactive blocker path (e.g. a permission prompt / AskUserQuestion-style interruption surfacing through an error tool_result) is still surfaced. If any genuine interactive blocker previously reached this branch, it is now silently dropped.
findings.suggestion: Add a test seeding an interactive-blocker-shaped error result and assert a card still renders; if it doesn't, restore a narrow branch for that case before the `continue`.

findings.finding: The spec's subrunner requirement is "the report shows a readable title with a link, not just a hash." The diff contains only a CSS size fix and a new test; no renderer change converts a hash-only subrunner title into the dispatch title/link. If the readable title already existed, this is fine, but if the shipped card showed a hash (as the spec implies), that half of the subrunner work is missing — the new test only checks that `card.text` renders and that an svg exists, which would pass against the old hash-only rendering too as long as text is passed through.
findings.suggestion: Verify against the mockup (board 2) what the subrunner row should show, and either add a renderer change or pin in the test that the rendered label is the dispatch title, not the agent id/hash.

findings.file: client/src/lib/missionActivityFeed.test.ts ("a failed read never produces an error card") and missionActivityFeedFields.test.ts ("attaches no error excerpt for a single failing non-test command")
findings.finding: These tests assert only negative invariants (`status !== "err"`, `detail === undefined`) which pass trivially if the reducer produces zero cards or drops them entirely — including a wrong implementation that also drops the turn's narration card. The fields test even acknowledges the card is dropped ("a wordless read-only card is dropped"). Nothing pins that the turn's own narration card still survives with its text, unlike the (g) test in missionActivityFeed.explanation.test.ts which does it properly.
findings.suggestion: In the single-failing-command cases, also assert the surviving card's text/explanation (like the (g) test does) so the "keep the turn's narration" behavior is pinned at every mutation site.

findings.finding: A failed command's card now keeps only whatever the turn wrote plus a bare command chip with no status marker — a card reading "Pushing the branch." + a `Bash: git push` chip is visually identical whether the push failed or succeeded. This is presumably the accepted M1 trade-off, but there is no test pinning that a successful and a failed command render distinguishably (or intentionally not), so a future change could reintroduce or over-remove status silently.
findings.suggestion: Add one test asserting the intended final shape for a failed command's card (text kept, no err pill) next to the successful twin.

findings.file: client/src/lib/missionActivityFeedTypes.ts — removal of `ActivityKind` "blocker" and `textLiteral`, plus deletion of `summarizeBlockerError`'s re-export in missionActivityFeedText.ts
findings.finding: These are hard removals of exported surface. Everything visible in the diff compiles, but any consumer outside the diff (other components, e2e helpers, or snapshot fixtures referencing `kind: "blocker"` / `textLiteral` / `summarizeBlockerError`) will now break at type-check or runtime. The e2e file updated here suggests there may be more stale references elsewhere in the e2e suite.
findings.suggestion: Run a repo-wide grep for `"blocker"`, `textLiteral`, and `summarizeBlockerError` before merging; update or remove any remaining fixtures.  Overall: the core M1 removal is implemented coherently and the deletion of the blocker machinery is thorough, but the spec's explicit "verify interactive blockers survive" requirement is not evidenced, and the subrunner "readable title" half may be missing. Ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Failed test output still renders directly in the feed through `card.detail`. The resolver continues attaching error excerpts to test cards, and the updated tests explicitly preserve this behavior. This only removes generic command errors; it does not satisfy “No error messages in the chat at all.”
findings.suggestion: Stop attaching or displaying failed tool output in feed cards, including test failures. Keep genuine interactive questions and any required test verdict indicators separate from terminal error text.

findings.finding: The new “compact (non-oversized)” test only checks that an SVG exists. It would pass if the sizing rule were removed entirely, reproducing the oversized checkmark this change is meant to fix.
findings.suggestion: Add a browser assertion that checks the rendered glyph dimensions against the link’s line size.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The generic blocker removal is implemented, but terminal error output still appears in the feed contrary to the explicit scope.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
